sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Social Commerce via Short Video Platforms

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law within a Federal State (Alberta applies the English common law tradition; federal constitutional supremacy and federal statutory overlay apply; Quebec civil law is not applicable)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 1 October 2014
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Convention Between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c 17, and its Regulations SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46 (money laundering and proceeds of crime offences); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, Part 2.1 (Unlimited Liability Corporation provisions) and Part 15 (books and records); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act (Alberta), SA 2022, c B-4.5 (beneficial ownership register obligations); FINTRAC guidance on beneficial ownership and politically exposed persons.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (or national ID) of each individual director and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's or director's country of residence plus the passport-issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) issued by the competent authority of the signatory state; if the state is not party to the Apostille Convention, Consular Legalization through Global Affairs Canada Authentication Services or the Embassy of Canada in the state of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Existence / Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder that is an intermediate or parent entity (e.g., a ByteDance group affiliate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registrar of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed by Global Affairs Canada attestation where required for provincial records; otherwise Consular Legalization at the Canadian Embassy in the relevant jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Consent to Act as Director for each ULC director executing in a foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the director's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization following the same rule as the passport bundle; if executed within Canada, domestic notarization alone suffices

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney / agency agreement appointing the Alberta incorporation agent and registered office service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of the UBO or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization via the Embassy of Canada in the relevant jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English translation of any non-English corporate records (e.g., Chinese-language articles of incorporation or shareholder register of the parent group)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified professional translator or translation company providing a sworn affidavit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's affidavit notarized, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the translator is located outside Canada; translations prepared inside Canada require no consular step for the Alberta registry

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and ongoing (not less than annually, plus event-driven re-screening) screening of all directors, UBOs, officers, and authorized signatories against: the UN Security Council Consolidated List; Canada's Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act; the OFAC SDN list (advisory, applicable because TikTok Shop payout and USD clearing rails touch the US financial system); UK and EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (advisory); FATF public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists; and domestic/foreign Politically Exposed Person (PEP) databases covering heads of state, ministers, senior judges, senior military officers, state-owned enterprise executives, and their family members and close associates. Standard Customer Due Diligence (CDD) under the PCMLTFA and Regulations SOR/2002-184 applies without exemption for low-risk retail models: verify identity, business intent, and source of funds; maintain beneficial ownership records; report suspicious transactions to FINTRAC where grounds exist; and apply Enhanced Due Diligence for PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions. The Low_Risk_Standard social-commerce classification does not remove these obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Access (corporateaccess.gov.ab.ca) and the authorized registry agent network performing NUANS name searches under Service Alberta supervision
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the operative language of the Alberta Corporate Registry; French-language names are permitted so long as the mandatory ULC legal element is included. Non-Latin script names are not accepted as the registered corporate name; any foreign-language name must be romanized/transliterated into Latin characters with a certified transliteration. The corporate name must comprise (1) a distinctive element, (2) an optional descriptive element, and (3) the mandatory legal element: 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée', or 'SRI'. Numerals, punctuation, and recognizable English or French words are permitted; meaningless letter strings are accepted if the NUANS search demonstrates distinctiveness.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Alberta (when used in a manner likely to mislead as to government affiliation or sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS name search report is valid for 90 days from the date of issue; no statutory extension exists, and if the Articles of Incorporation are not filed within that window a new NUANS report must be commissioned. Upon name rejection: (1) the registry issues a rejection notice stating the reason code; (2) the applicant may file a written Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar of Corporations (Service Alberta) within 30 days of the rejection notice; (3) alternatively or additionally, the applicant may commission a new NUANS search adding a distinguishing word or amending the descriptive element; (4) if administrative review is unsuccessful, the decision may be challenged by judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta, with the originating application required within 30 days of the final administrative decision; and (5) counsel is advised to reserve a backup name under the same or a parallel NUANS report to avoid incorporation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with conditions: the registered office must be a physical street address in Alberta and cannot be a post office box; a commercial virtual-office or registered-agent address in Calgary or Edmonton satisfies the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, s 101. A separate records address is required under section 102 for corporate books and records. This structure is acceptable for the TikTok Shop e-commerce model with no physical storefront, but Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST) audit notices must be reachable at the records address, and Alberta consumer-protection filings must list an Alberta address for service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, approximately 5% probability within the first three years of operation. The Alberta Corporate Registry does not conduct unannounced physical inspections of standard-risk retail entities. FINTRAC compliance examinations are risk-scheduled and are normally desk-based for the Low_Risk_Standard e-commerce tier; CRA audits proceed by written demand for records and do not involve physical raids on virtual offices. Retention of a registered agent ensures service of any statutory demand at the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search report (one preferred name plus one backup name)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Service Alberta / authorized NUANS provider (corporate registry agent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation filing — Unlimited Liability Corporation (electronic filing)
Registered office address plus records address service (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider / registered agent (Calgary or Edmonton)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (approximately C$175 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal opinion — ULC pass-through eligibility and Canadian tax characterization for non-resident shareholders
AML/CFT compliance program setup — written policies, FINTRAC regime, beneficial ownership register, risk assessment, CDD procedures
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance consultant / external law firm

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening subscription (first year, covering 2–3 UBO entities with quarterly refresh)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial sanctions-screening data provider (e.g., Refinitiv/LSEG, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization of three UBO/director documentary sets
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaries public abroad, provincial authentication authority (Alberta Justice / Global Affairs Canada)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document fees and market notarial benchmark (approximately USD 120 per document set)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified English translation of foreign-language corporate and identity documents
Corporate minute book, share certificates, and ULC statutory registers (electronic format)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended: ss 5-12 (incorporation and articles), s 15.1 (election to be an Unlimited Liability Corporation), s 101 (registered office), s 113 (directors), s 24 (share consideration). The Canada Business Corporations Act is not applicable; the ULC is a provincial entity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, 4th Floor, 10155-102 Street, Edmonton, AB; filings accepted online through the Corporate Registry system or accredited service providers.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed with the Registrar under the ABCA, together with Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form 3 (Notice of Directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or deposit requirement for incorporation; shares may be issued without par value for consideration fixed by the board per ABCA s 24.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1. That the incorporation of the Company under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) as an Unlimited Liability Corporation be ratified, and the Certificate of Incorporation is accepted. 2. That the shares subscribed by the incorporator be allotted and issued, fully paid, as recorded in the share register. 3. That the registered office of the Company be established at the principal office address in Alberta, and the record depositary be confirmed. 4. That By-law No. 1 be adopted. 5. That [President], [Secretary] and [Chief Financial Officer] be appointed officers of the Company. 6. That the officers be authorized to open bank accounts, onboard TikTok Shop payment rails, register CRA accounts, and execute ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Name Search Unit (NuANS), accessible through accredited service providers and online registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names for a NuANS pre-approved name search. Each name must include the mandatory suffix 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Verify the selected name is distinct from existing Alberta and federal corporate names and registered trademarks.
required_dossiers: List of three proposed corporate names with ULC suffix
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for confusing similarity, file a new search with alternative names or provide letters of consent from the conflicting name holder; the Registrar may approve a distinctive name upon sufficient justification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Incorporation and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel (internal drafting); Alberta Corporate Registry as eventual filing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 Articles of Incorporation electing ULC status under ABCA s 15.1(2) with an express statement that shareholders have unlimited liability. Define share structure, list the registered office address (physical address, no post office box) and identify first directors. Obtain signed Form 25 consents from each director.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Articles of Incorporation (draft, executed by incorporator)
Form 25 Consent to Act as Director for each director
Registered office address and landlord consent
Share structure and authorized capital summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Internal correction of drafting defects before filing; if the Registrar later queries the articles, submit a revised Form 1 with an explanatory letter within 30 days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (online or Edmonton office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit executed Form 1 Articles of Incorporation with the CAD 275 filing fee, accompanied by initial Form 2 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form 3 (Notice of Directors). Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation with an Alberta incorporation number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, remedy noted deficiencies and resubmit within 30 days; a refusal by the Registrar may be appealed to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting and Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal statutory governance; corporate secretary administers the minute book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or execute unanimous written consent. Adopt By-law No. 1, approve share subscription and allotment, ratify the registered office, appoint officers, approve the corporate seal, and authorize bank account opening and payment rail onboarding.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma board resolutions and written consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any procedural defect in notice or quorum may be cured by a unanimous directors' consent or a subsequent ratification resolution adopted by the full board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency - Business Registration Online; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance (Alberta Corporate Tax); Workers' Compensation Board - Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the CRA for a nine-digit Business Number and GST/HST program account, which is mandatory once taxable sales exceed CAD 30,000 or voluntarily if seeking input tax credits. Open an Alberta corporate income tax account and, if employees are hired, a CRA payroll deductions account and a WCB-Alberta account.
required_dossiers: RC1 Business Number registration form or online attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA application is queried, correct director information and resubmit via the CRA Business Window at 1-800-959-5525; late registration penalties may apply, and voluntary GST registration can be backdated with justification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal business licence office of the registered municipality (e.g., City of Edmonton or City of Calgary); Alberta Safety Codes Authority; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal Business Licence covering e-commerce retail and warehousing at the registered premises. Obtain an occupancy permit and fire safety inspection for the warehouse or office, comply with the Alberta Fire Code, and complete an OH&S hazard assessment if employees are engaged. TikTok Shop social commerce requires no additional provincial operating licence.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement for warehouse or registered office
Floor plan and building occupancy permit
Fire safety inspection request and OH&S hazard assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is denied for zoning or fire code deficiencies, remedy the occupancy issues, seek a variance from the municipal development authority, or relocate to a compliant premises; appeal any denial to the subdivision and development appeal board within 21 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing board regulates social commerce retail; the operative licence issuer is the municipal business licence office of the registered municipality, with supporting clearance from the Alberta Safety Codes Authority and Alberta Occupational Health and Safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence for E-Commerce Retail and Warehousing (General, Non-Regulated Activity); no province-wide statutory operating licence is prescribed for NAICS 454110 / ISIC 4791.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas, Environmental Assessment and Approvals Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt: pure e-commerce retail and warehousing is not a designated activity under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12; no EIA registration or approval is required. A municipal stormwater drainage permit may apply to warehouse parking areas.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or VOC-emitting equipment; sanitary effluent discharged to municipal sewer under municipal by-law limits; packaging cardboard and plastics diversion under municipal recycling by-laws and Alberta recycling regulations; HVAC refrigerants regulated under the federal Ozone-Depleting Substances and Halocarbons Regulations; any battery or e-waste handling requires Extended Producer Responsibility compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: inspection and permit per the Alberta Fire Code (Safety Codes Act) covering fire alarms, extinguishers, egress and storage racking. Structural: Alberta Building Code occupancy permit confirming floor load capacity for e-commerce shelving. Occupational: OH&S hazard assessment, first-aid kit and employer registration with Alberta Occupational Health and Safety, plus a WCB-Alberta clearance letter if employees are hired. Home-based operations require a municipal home occupation permit and a residential fire safety check.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, acting as the sole federal tax collection authority for income tax and GST/HST; Alberta corporate income tax is assessed federally under the Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement and the Alberta Corporate Tax Act; corporate law filings are made with the Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta); CRA portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html (My Business Account).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the unlimited liability corporation (ULC) with Alberta Corporate Registry (or extra-provincially register a BC/NS ULC), obtaining the Alberta organization number. Step 2: Register with CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1 to obtain the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) and program accounts, including RT0001 (corporate income tax) and RT0001/RZ identity for GST/HST. Step 3: For non-resident-owned ULCs, use the CRA non-resident simplified GST/HST registration process; non-resident shareholders are not issued separate Canadian TINs, and the ULC's BN is the sole statutory tax identifier. Step 4: Enroll in My Business Account, appoint a Canadian fiscal agent/address, and link TikTok Shop seller payouts to the ULC's GST/HST account before commencing retail operations; no statutory licence or minimum capital is required for ISIC 4791/NAICS 454110 social commerce retailing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a provincial ULC is statutorily a 'taxable Canadian corporation' under Income Tax Act s. 89(1), subject to Part I corporate income tax (combined 23% general corporate rate: 15% federal + 8% Alberta) and to full GST/HST registration, filing, and remittance obligations; however, the ULC structure is Pass_Through_Eligible only upon a valid ITA s. 114.1 election, as described below.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available: (i) Form RC232 election under Income Tax Act subsection 114.1(1), deeming the ULC to be a partnership for Canadian tax purposes where foreign members are taxed on a look-through basis; (ii) United States check-the-box election on Form 8832 under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3, classifying the Canadian ULC as a disregarded entity or partnership for U.S. federal tax purposes; (iii) domestic hybrid-mismatch rules and Canada-U.S. Treaty limitation-on-benefits provisions operate to prevent double non-taxation from abusive use of the ULC election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta is a non-participating province with no provincial sales tax (PST) or HST, so only the 5% federal GST applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in the preceding 12 calendar months (general small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 240(2) and s. 242.1); non-resident vendors and digital platform operators (including TikTok Shop as marketplace/distribution platform) become mandatory GST/HST registrants when supplies into Canada reach or exceed C$30,000 in a calendar year, with the simplified non-resident GST/HST regime available regardless of Canadian presence.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance, no API-based invoice authorization, and no digital stamping. E-invoicing is voluntary and follows the Pan-Canadian e-invoice standard 'Riel' (Peppol BIS-based XML); CRA does not pre-clear invoices. Mandatory electronic filing applies to GST/HST registrants with annual taxable revenues exceeding C$1 million; all returns must otherwise be filed electronically via CRA's My Business Account or approved third-party software, and payments must be remitted electronically within the statutory due date (generally one month after the end of the monthly/quarterly reporting period).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act where: (i) the ULC is GST/HST-registered; (ii) physical goods sold through TikTok Shop are exported, or made available to the non-resident buyer outside Canada, and are removed from Canada promptly under a genuine contract of sale; (iii) the ULC maintains contemporaneous evidence of export; and (iv) services supplied to non-residents (including digital platform facilitation or offshore advertising) are not made in the course of a GST/HST taxable supply in Canada and are for consumption exclusively outside Canada. Supplies of digital content or goods delivered to TikTok Shop consumers within Canada are standard-rated at 5% and must be included in the GST/HST return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System/CES) for shipments exceeding CAD 2,000 or controlled goods
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing export from Canada to the destination country
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank foreign-exchange receipt) evidencing receipt of export sale proceeds
TikTok Shop seller payout statements and platform transaction reports identifying buyer jurisdiction and shipment tracking
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA's digital-economy and non-resident audit teams treat marketplace sellers as high-visibility; zero-rating claims are systematically matched against customs declarations, transport documents, and platform payout data. Failure to repatriate FX proceeds within 180 days is treated as a red flag that the export may be fictitious, triggering GAAR and retrospective clawback. On disqualification, CRA may reassess within four years (or seven years on waiver), disallow the 0% rate, recover the net GST/HST with interest, and impose penalties under ETA s. 285 equal to the greater of C$250 and 25% of the tax amount; criminal prosecution is available under ETA s. 239 and ITA s. 239(1) with fines up to C$100,000 and imprisonment up to five years; all export records and FX remittance evidence must be retained for at least six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and, for financial-sector conduct and AML supervision, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada does not maintain a dedicated foreign exchange control administration; the Bank of Canada operates the national monetary framework while the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act provide the legal basis for the Canadian dollar as legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada has accepted Article VIII obligations under the IMF Articles of Agreement, and there are no exchange control approvals, surrender requirements, or central bank permits required for inbound equity subscriptions, intercompany loans, or outbound trade settlements. Profit remittance and dividend distributions from an Alberta ULC to a non-resident parent or shareholder are freely permitted, subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under sections 212 and 215 of the Income Tax Act (Canada). For a ULC that is treated as a taxable Canadian corporation, dividends paid to a U.S. shareholder may qualify for a reduced withholding tax rate under the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention if the recipient provides a valid IRS Form W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E certificate of residency. Alberta imposes no separate provincial exchange control or capital repatriation restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Canada does not impose statutory export proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion into Canadian dollars, or prescribed repatriation timelines. An Alberta exporter may lawfully hold export proceeds in foreign currency accounts at Canadian authorized foreign currency dealers. For tax purposes, the exporter must report foreign currency gains and losses under subsection 39(1) of the Income Tax Act (Canada), accrue foreign interest under subsection 12(1)(c), and preserve books, records, export invoices, bank settlement advices, and FX contracts for at least six years pursuant to subsection 230(1) of the Income Tax Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium as a supplementary payment and settlement rail, Low as the primary treasury relationship. A foreign electronic money institution (EMI) or fintech such as Wise Inc. may operate in Canada as a money services business (MSB), requiring registration with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. It cannot accept Canadian deposits or carry on banking activities without a Bank Act authorization, and it cannot directly clear through Payments Canada. Wise B2B is viable for cross-border supplier disbursements and TikTok Shop payout aggregation only in tandem with a Tier-1 Canadian bank account. The Alberta ULC must maintain a Canadian-dollar operating account and a USD foreign-currency sub-account at a Schedule I bank for treasury concentration; fintech rails are used strictly for corridor optimization, not as a liquidity custody layer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC guidance does not impose an absolute statutory requirement for physical in-branch appearance; directors may generally satisfy customer due diligence through a single-process or dual-process remote identity verification using video conferencing, electronic identity proofing, and certified documentation. In practice, however, Tier-1 Canadian banks require an in-person or notarized/presented interview for ULC entities with non-resident beneficial owners because the unlimited liability structure increases underwriting complexity. A Canadian-resident director, officer, or authorized signatory is strongly recommended. Non-resident directors should expect enhanced due diligence, dual-source identity verification, a physical signing appointment at a branch where reasonably possible, and a bank-specific director attestation form. Remote opening is generally possible where the director is a Canadian resident and all beneficial owners are verifiable through equivalent regulated financial institutions in FATF-compliant jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or U.S. parent owning 100% of an Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation, with the corporate designation 'ULC' triggering an unusual legal form assessment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified articles of incorporation, long-form certificate from Alberta Corporate Registry, by-laws, unanimous shareholder agreement, register of directors with full residential addresses and passports, corporate structure chart up to ultimate individual beneficial owners, reserve of source of wealth documents, notarized legal opinion explaining the ULC tax classification, and the commercial rationale for using unlimited liability rather than an Alberta Ltd.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Social media retail via TikTok Shop generating high-velocity, low-ticket transaction flows with capital deployed through payouts that arrive as aggregated settlement files rather than individual customer payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed TikTok Shop seller agreement, TikTok Shop payout statements, merchant dashboard authenticated screenshots, reconciliation of gross sales to net settlement after fees, chargeback and refund reports, inventory purchase invoices from suppliers, logistics tracking, customs entry documents, and a written compliance narrative demonstrating that settlement funds originate from licensed e-commerce activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire traffic to PRC-based suppliers, Hong Kong intermediaries, and U.S. distribution platforms inconsistent with declared ISIC 4791 retail activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed trade payment matrix mapping each counterparty to purchase orders and supplier invoices; intercompany agreements supported by transfer pricing documentation; FATCA and CRS self-certifications; W-8/W-9 forms; a copy of the Treasury/Accounts Payable policy; and foreign exchange forward contracts evidencing the underlying trade exposure, if any.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party fintech corridors (Wise B2B, TikTok settlements) and foreign exchange forwards executed through a non-Canadian counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC registration certificate or confirmation of MSB status for the relevant Canadian fintech corridor; FATF-jurisdiction licensing evidence for foreign counterparties; ISDA Master Agreement or negotiated master terms; due diligence file on the counterparty; transaction monitoring statements; and an independent legal opinion confirming that the ULC has not engaged in unlicensed financial services activity in Canada.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital injections from non-resident shareholders should be executed by SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the investor's bank to the ULC's Canadian-dollar operating account at a Schedule I Canadian bank. The Beneficiary field must identify the ULC legal name; the Remittance Information field must state 'Share Capital Subscription' or 'Paid-up Capital Injection' together with the Alberta Corporate Registry number and the date of the directors' resolution authorizing issuance. Canada requires no exchange control permit; however, if the foreign investor acquires control of an existing Alberta business or the transaction meets the monetary thresholds in the Investment Canada Act, a post-closing investment notification or application for review may be required. The supporting verification package should include board resolutions, share subscription agreements, share certificate ledger, source-of-funds letters from the remitting bank, and Form T106 (if any intercompany cross-border loans or transfers are made). For shareholder loans, a written demand loan agreement with arm's length interest rate is required to avoid deemed interest and Canadian withholding tax consequences.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails for outbound trade disbursements are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire settlements to supplier bank accounts in USD, EUR, or CNY, relying on the ULC's foreign currency sub-account and its bank's correspondent network; (ii) documentary letters of credit issued by a Canadian commercial bank subject to UCP 600 for bulk inventory purchases from PRC-based suppliers; (iii) Payments Canada Automated Clearing Settlement System for domestic CAD payables; and (iv) commercial cross-border payout rails such as Wise B2B for low-value supplier payments whose settlement requirements fit fintech corridor rules. Each wire instruction should include the invoice number, purchase order reference, and ISIC/NAICS business descriptor. For supplier disbursements involving Chinese renminbi, the Canadian bank may require a non-deliverable forward or CNH account arrangement because CAD/CNY convertibility of direct CNY funds is subject to corresponding bank availability. TikTok Shop advertising and fulfillment costs may be paid via commercial card or ACH using operating account proceeds, but all settlement funds should be reconciled to the supplier ledger and not commingled with prohibited cryptoassets.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts executed with a Canadian Schedule I bank under ISDA 1998 FX Definitions, covering the ULC's receipt streams from TikTok Shop USD settlements and payables to U.S. distributors.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNH or USD/CNY for PRC supplier payables where direct CNY settlement is restricted; the NDF must be referenced to a recognized CNH fixing and booked through a licensed international bank acting as an offshore RMB clearing participant.
Cross-currency basis swaps (CAD/USD and USD/CNH) used to convert TikTok Shop USD revenue into CAD or to transform fixed-rate liability exposures into floating-rate obligations.

Plain-vanilla CAD/USD exchange-traded options or over-the-counter vanilla options, permitted only when covered by underlying inventory purchase commitments and documented under IFRS 9 hedge accounting with contemporaneous hedge designation and effectiveness testing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation; no extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties apply after the 60-day window; failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Registrar to dissolve the ULC administratively. The directors may also be subject to enforcement and restoration costs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within six months after the taxation year-end of the ULC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger a penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; additional penalties apply for repeated failures, and CRA may assess interest on outstanding balances and pursue director liability for certain unpaid amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filers, due within three months after the fiscal year-end; installment and quarterly filing rules apply depending on annual taxable revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled or late remitted GST/HST attracts daily arrears interest and late-filing penalties; willful non-filing can result in fines and prosecution under the Excise Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No public filing; maintained at registered office for inspection by Alberta Corporate Registry and law-enforcement authorities upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Reviewed and updated annually as of the incorporation anniversary; changes must be recorded within 15 days of any transfer or relevant event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain an adequate register of individuals with significant control is an offence under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and may result in fines and prosecution; directors may be personally liable for violations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The Alberta Business Corporations Act requires an auditor annually unless all shareholders consent in writing to waive the audit for that fiscal year. There is no revenue-based statutory threshold; a distributing or public ULC must appoint an auditor. The waiver must be unanimous and cannot be mandated by a simple shareholder majority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; a private ULC may prepare financial statements in accordance with Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ULCs must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. No annual filing of the register is made to the Alberta Corporate Registry; however, the register must be current, must record any shareholding transfer and change in significant control within 15 days, must be reviewed at least annually, and must be made available to enforcement authorities on request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 to USD 650 per year depending on registered office location and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 12,000 per year depending on transaction volume, complexity of TikTok Shop retail operations, and audit depth required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% (15% federal general rate + 8% Alberta general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in Canada. A preferential 11% combined federal+Alberta small business rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta) is available for up to C$500,000 of taxable income only to Canadian-controlled private corporations; an Alberta ULC controlled by a non-resident parent will not qualify for the small business deduction. SR&ED investment tax credits (ITC) and the inter-provincial income-allocation rules may reduce the effective Alberta rate to a lower blended rate depending on revenue sourcing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (CRA) filed electronically via approved EFILE/NetFile for Corporations, using CRA-certified tax software (mandatory e-filing for most T2 filers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal period generally not exceeding 12 months; no quarterly corporate income tax returns required, but quarterly instalments may apply).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed no later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Balance of tax due is generally due the later of 2 months after year-end or 3 months after year-end for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations; for non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada, the filing deadline remains 6 months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered address, business number, incorporation jurisdiction, fiscal period end and contact information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled Alberta ULC must enter its CRA business number, the Canadian representative information, and the foreign parent corporation's name and country. The form must clearly identify the ULC as an Alberta unlimited liability company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and commissions from TikTok Shop retail operations, including live-commerce product sales, tip and commission revenue, and fulfillment fees, net of returns and chargebacks.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ULC carries on business in Canada via a permanent establishment (PE) in Alberta, all attributable gross sales revenue must be reported and allocated to Alberta under the federal–provincial income allocation rules (Schedule 5).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting business expenses, inventory adjustments, amortization/Capital Cost Allowance, and any prior non-capital loss carryovers (20-year window).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The ULC, if resident in Canada for tax purposes, must report worldwide taxable income; if it is a non-resident corporation, only income from its Canadian pe is reportable. A hybrid/ULC election under the US check-the-box rules does not alter Canadian CRA treatment as a taxable corporate person.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal 15% + Alberta 8% General rate, computed on Line 200; treaty-based reductions and foreign tax credits are applied below.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Even if the ULC is wholly owned by a non-resident parent, the 23% combined statutory rate applies to all Canadian-source taxable income attributed to the Alberta PE and to other Canadian sourcing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 450 — Net tax payable / balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessed income tax after foreign tax credits, federal/provincial rebates, investment tax credits, instalment payments, and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent shareholders should ensure that all cross-border transactions (royalties, interest, fees) are properly reported on T106, and that Part XIII withholding tax on profit repatriation is handled in the Form T2 return and related information schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of outstanding balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (minimum C$100); second and subsequent offence: 10% plus 2% per month. Penalties apply on failure to file required T106/T2081 information returns and may also trigger a s.163(2) gross-negligence penalty if repetition is wilful.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties_summary: Late filing: 5% of outstanding balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (minimum C$100); second and subsequent offence: 10% plus 2% per month. Penalties apply on failure to file required T106/T2081 information returns and may also trigger a s.163(2) gross-negligence penalty if repetition is wilful.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory Canadian Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by an Alberta ULC to a non-resident person is 25%. Treaty relief may reduce the rate depending on the parent’s jurisdiction and ownership percentage (e.g., Canada–China DTA: 15% general, 5% for beneficial owner holding ≥10% of voting shares; Canada–US DTA: 15% general, 5% for beneficial corporate owner holding ≥10% voting rights).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the payor (the ULC) with a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority and submit completed Form NR301 (Application for a Reduction of Withholding Tax on Dividends, Interest, Royalties, etc.) to the CRA. The payor must rely on the approved reduction and withhold at the treaty rate. If excess withholding is required at the outset, the non-resident may later file Form NR302 (Application for a Refund of Part XIII Tax) with a TRC and proof of residence for the relevant period. For payments routed through an intermediary or a hybrid/partnership blocker, the beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility analysis must be included in the T106 disclosure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25%. For interest paid by an Alberta ULC to a related non-resident lender, most Canadian tax treaties reduce the rate to 10% or 0% (e.g., 10% under Canada–China DTA; 0% under Canada–US DTA for arm’s length or unidentified beneficial owners). Royalties for trademarks/copyright/licensed content (e.g., TikTok algorithm or brand IP) face a 25% statutory rate; bilateral treaties commonly reduce to 10% (Canada–US: 10%; Canada–China: 10%; payments may be exempt as business profits under a PE threshold if the intellectual property is used in Canada through a PE located in Alberta).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer-pricing records (equivalent to a Local File) are mandatory in Canada when the aggregate value of all reportable transactions (purchase, sales, services, interest, royalty) between the Alberta ULC and non-resident non-arm’s length persons in a fiscal year exceeds C$1,000,000. A Master File is required where the Canadian corporation belongs to a multinational enterprise group with consolidated group revenue of at least C$750 million; Country-by-Country reporting follows the same group threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Alberta and federal Canada do not apply the UAE/ Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). However, the Income Tax Act socio-economic anti-avoidance rules (GAAR, s.245) and substance-over-form doctrine effectively require the ULC to maintain meaningful physical and economic presence in Alberta (e.g., real employees, office/warehouse or supply-chain functions, inventory risk, independent board decisions). An artificial transaction without economic substance will be recharacterized, and a ULC used solely as a dormant pass-through shell will be denied treaty benefits and PTEP (post-bound rate) under the substance-based test in s.94.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting TikTok-Shop gross sales, underreporting live-commerce commissions, or claiming fictitious deductions for personal expenses in the T2 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s.239(1) — criminal fine not less than 100% and not more than 200% of the tax evaded, plus imprisonment for up to 5 years. Civil sanctions under s.163(2) impose a gross-negligence penalty equal to 50% of the amount of the understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize, approve, or acquiesce to the filing of a false return may be prosecuted personally for the offence (s.239(1.1)). The court may order a travel ban, cease- and-desist, restitution, and imprisonment of the responsible officer; civil liability under s.160 can also reach the director as a transferee.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the unlimited liability structure as a shell that has no employees, no premises, or no real economic activity in Alberta, bypassing Part XIII withholding tax on outbound dividends, or shifting TIKTOK Shop retail profits to the offshore parent through a flow-through 'hybrid' classification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s.245(2) GAAR denying tax-benefit recharacterization (the transaction will be taxed as if the substantive step had not occurred), additional fines/interest, and transfer-pricing penalties under s.247(9). CRA can also reclassify the ULC as a conduit and impose Part XIII withholding on deemed dividends (s.84).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed to s.160 debtor-liability, an administrative assessment as a transferor, and in egregious situations, criminal liability for participation in an avoidance transaction under s.239. Courts may issue injunctions and travel bans and may convert the ULC’s unlimited liability into a personal guarantee of the director (under AB Business Corporations Act an ULC’s shareholders are jointly and severally liable, although directors are not automatically, but dishonesty triggers officer-complicity liability).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling physical or virtual products to, or paying fees/services from, a non-arm’s-length foreign TikTok parent/licensor at a price that materially deviates from the arm's-length price, such as underpricing inventory to shift profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA will re-determine the price under s.247(2); a proportionate penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment is imposed unless the taxpayer has made bona fide, documented, contemporaneous efforts to establish arm’s-length pricing (s.247(9)). The adjustment also accrues arrears interest and may trigger a gross-negligence penalty if concealment is found.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in the mispricing are jointly and severally liable for penalties assessed under s.247(9) and may be named in a civil action for restitution. Repeated or fraudulent mispricing can subject officers to criminal tax evasion charges (s.239) and personal tax liens on their property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Information Returns / AML & FINTRAC Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form T106 (Schedule of Non-Arm’s Length Transactions with Non-Residents) or failing to report large cross-border electronic transfers related to TikTok Shop payouts to/receipts from foreign payment service providers (e.g., Wise B2B), or failing to register as a money-services business (MSB) where crypto/stablecoins are involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s.162(7), penalties of C$25 per day (up to C$2,500) for each unreported transaction; under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), a corporation can face administrative monetary penalties up to C$500,000 per violation, and failure to register as an MSB attracts a separate penalty and stop-re work order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for FINTRAC penalties, but directors who direct, participate in, or approve non-filing are treated as operating the business under the PCMLTFA and may be personally assessed. A court order may freeze the director’s personal assets as a travel ban until unfiled returns are produced; entrepreneurial disregard of filing obligations can trigger a custody order for contempt of court and imprisonment.
